title: The hunter's arrow
hookLine: a hunter's arrow strikes Krishna, and Krishna sends the hunter to heaven
carry: god's grace reaches even the one who wounded him
tomorrow: one name in Vishnu's line surprises people. whose, and why?

cards: A phone knocked into a pool. A borrowed car with a fresh dent. A friend who did real damage without meaning to and now can't stop saying sorry.

The Bhagavata Purana tells one of these at the very end of Krishna's life. A hunter named Jara sees something move among the leaves near the sea, takes it for a deer, and lets an arrow fly. It isn't a deer.
It's Krishna's foot. Jara runs up, sees whom he has hit, and falls at his feet, shaking. And the first thing Krishna says to him is: don't be afraid.

teach.h: A CLAN FALLS APART BY THE SEA.
teach.b: The scene is already sorrowful before the arrow flies. Krishna's own clan, the Yadus, has torn itself apart in a drunken quarrel by the sea, and his brother Balarama has already left the world.
Krishna sits quietly under a tree, one foot resting across his thigh.

teach.h: AN ARROW, MEANT FOR A DEER.
teach.b: Then the arrow. Jara begs him: I did this without knowing. Punish me.
Krishna's answer turns the whole scene.

teach.h: DON'T BE AFRAID. THIS WAS MY WISH.
teach.b: Don't be afraid, Jara. Get up. This happened by my own wish.
And then the part that stuns people: Krishna sends the hunter to heaven. Jara circles him, bows, and is carried up. Look at what Krishna doesn't do.
He doesn't make Jara earn it, or wait for a better apology.

teach.h: GRACE REACHES THE ONE WHO WOUNDED HIM.
teach.b: The wounded one is the one who gives. Many teachers read this as grace, kripa in Sanskrit: the Lord's gift, given freely, reaching even the hand that hurt him.
And by my own wish says one more thing Hindus hold about Krishna: his coming and going are his lila, his play, not something done to him.
Then he leaves the world, and the Bhagavata adds a line that matters for these weeks: on the day he went, the age of Kali came in.

how: Tradition links Krishna's departure to the Gujarat coast near Prabhasa, where pilgrims visit a shrine at the place associated with Jara's arrow.

games.q: your little cousin hears the ending and says: the hunter should've been punished! what does Krishna do in the Bhagavata?
o: tells him not to fear and sends him to heaven: grace, freely given.
curses him, so everyone learns to be careful with arrows.
forgives him only after years of penance and apology.
games.why: Jara begged to be punished. Krishna said don't be afraid, this was my wish, and sent him to heaven. many teachers call it kripa, grace.

practice: Fold your hands. Many Hindus close their worship with a short prayer asking forgiveness for anything done wrong, knowingly or not. Say it once in your own words: for whatever I did without knowing, forgive me.
Then, on each breath out, let someone who hurt you without meaning to come to mind, and hold them in that same light. If you don't pray, simply sit with both.

wordCard.voice: Krishna: struck by a hunter's stray arrow at the end of his life, he told the hunter don't be afraid, and sent him to heaven.

orig.note: Sanskrit: don't be afraid, Krishna's first words to the hunter Jara.
